title: The hand-off check pads its count on macOS, so a dirty repository reads as "       2 paths"
foundBy: campaign CI on f1eb71f: build-test failed on macos-15-intel and macos-arm64, and passed on Linux and WSL2
details:
`HandoffCheckScript` counts a repository's uncommitted paths with `wc -l`. BSD `wc`, which macOS ships, pads the count with spaces, so the check printed `DIRTY\tapp\t       2\ta.txt` and the member read `~/app has work not committed (       2 paths, the first a.txt)`. GNU `wc` prints a bare number, so Linux, where every member runs, was right. `TestTheHandoffCheckReadsGitAndTheHandoff` failed on both macOS runners, in six of its sixteen cases: every one that prints a count.

The member reads the sentence and the campaign decides on the count, so a padded count is a wrong sentence and nothing worse. The script should print a bare number on either `wc`, and the reader should trim what it is given.
